These fixtures are CONSTRUCTED for tests -- they are NOT real SEC data.

They follow the field list documented on the SEC Fails-to-Deliver Data
page (https://www.sec.gov/data-research/sec-markets-data/fails-deliver-data):

    SETTLEMENT DATE (8 digits) | CUSIP (9 chars) | SYMBOL (10 chars) |
    QUANTITY (FAILS) | DESCRIPTION (30 chars) | PRICE

  "The data items are provided as a 'pipe delimited' text file."

Each row is the OUTSTANDING BALANCE of fails as of SETTLEMENT DATE, not a
count of new fails that day -- see sec_ftd.py's module docstring for the
exact quotes this constraint comes from.

Files:
  good.txt              -- well-formed file, header row + 3 rows (3 CUSIPs).
  empty.txt              -- header row only, no data rows.
  malformed.txt          -- header row, one well-formed row, one row with
                            a non-numeric QUANTITY, and one row with a
                            wrong field count.
  revised_same_date.txt  -- same (settlement date, CUSIP) key as one row
                            in good.txt but a different QUANTITY, used to
                            exercise idempotent-write behavior (a second
                            pull must not duplicate or silently overwrite
                            the already-stored balance).
